attributeDefinition: Date the seine sample was collected.

Unique identifier of the seine sample (one seine haul or set of hauls at one location on one date): the source period (1997-2001, 2008-2014 or 2015-2025) and the sample ID in that period's source database (the seine ID for 1997-2001), joined by an underscore, e.g. 2015-2025_1500. Source IDs repeat across periods, so the period prefix is needed to identify a sample. More than one sample can share a date and location (repeat hauls).

Name of the sampling location as recorded in the source data. Raw names are kept (spelling and format vary by source period and include side-channel, bank and upstream/downstream qualifiers); use river_mile to group locations by site.

Feather River channel the location is in: LFC (Low Flow Channel, Fish Barrier Dam at river mile 67 to the Thermalito Afterbay Outlet at river mile 59), HFC (High Flow Channel; assumed to be the part upstream of the lower Yuba River, since the downstream part is coded separately) or HFC DS LYR (High Flow Channel downstream of the lower Yuba River). Not recorded for 1997-2014 data or a small number of 2015-2025 records.
Sampling gear type. All records are beach seine (SEIN); other gear types in the source data (nets, electrofishing) were removed.
Description of the beach seine used, by net length in feet (10, 25, 39, 50 or 100 foot beach seine with bag).

Rating of how the seine haul went, recorded by the crew: good (haul went smoothly), fair (haul went relatively smoothly but had to be stopped once or twice to free snags or remove rocks or debris), or poor (haul went poorly, with numerous stops and plenty of opportunity for fish to escape, but was completed). 'n/p' is entered in the source data for some records; REVIEW: assumed to be the protocol's 'no sample taken' category (haul could not be completed) - confirm.

Water temperature at the time of sampling. 1997-2001 values were recorded in degrees Fahrenheit and converted to Celsius (a recorded value of 0 was treated as not recorded); a single entry of 147 for sample 1628 was corrected to 17 per the data owner.

Secchi depth, recorded in 1997-2001 data only (source column 'sechi'). REVIEW: about 99% of values are 0, which likely means not recorded, and units are not documented - confirm units or remove this column.

Common name of the fish species (lower case) as standardized from source codes and spellings. Includes unidentified groups (e.g. unidentified juvenile minnow) and the composite 'sacramento pikeminnow or hardhead'. Chinook salmon and O. mykiss are not split by race or origin here; see run and adipose_clipped. Blank where no fish were caught.
missingValueCodeExplanation: No fish caught or species not recorded

attributeDefinition: Fork length of the fish, in millimeters (1997-2001: individual fish; 2008-2025: fish or length class counted in count). Per the survey report, a subsample of up to 50 fish of each salmonid species or run and up to 20 fish of each other species were measured per haul, with the remainder counted but not measured. Blank where fish were counted but not measured (a recorded length of 0 was set to missing).

Life stage of salmonids, assigned by the crew from external characteristics: yolk-sac fry (yolk sac clearly visible), fry (yolk sac not fully absorbed), parr (darkly pigmented with dark oval parr marks, yolk sac absorbed), silvery parr, between parr and smolt (intermediate: fading parr marks and some scale loss), smolt (parr marks highly faded or absent, bright silver color, heavy scale loss), or adult; 'n/p' as entered in the source data (assumed 'not provided'). Recorded for measured salmonids only.

Chinook salmon run (Fall, Spring, Late Fall, Winter or Unknown). Per the survey report, runs are assigned from fork length and date using the length-at-date criteria of the Sacramento River Daily Length Table (Greene 1992). Blank for all non-Chinook records.

Length of the seine haul. Recorded in meters: the 1997-2001 field datasheet gives seine area length, width and depth in meters, and the 2022 datasheet lets the crew record meters or feet, with 2008-2025 database values in meters (values entered in feet appear to have been converted at 3.28 ft per meter). Source columns: 'length' (1997-2001) and 'bs_start_length' (2008-2025). REVIEW: typical values differ between periods (median about 20 in 1997-2001, 14.5 in 2008-2014 and 29 in 2015-2025), so confirm that the 1997-2001 and later fields measure the same thing.

Width of the seine haul. Recorded in meters: the 1997-2001 field datasheet gives seine area length, width and depth in meters, and the 2022 datasheet lets the crew record meters or feet, with 2008-2025 database values in meters (values entered in feet appear to have been converted at 3.28 ft per meter). Source columns: 'width' (1997-2001) and 'bs_close_width' (2008-2025). REVIEW: typical values differ between periods (median about 10 in 1997-2001 and about 1 or less afterward), so confirm that the fields measure the same thing. 2015-2025 values are 0 to 0.6 and about 98% are missing.

Distance from the bank that the seine was deployed, in meters. Values have the same range and typical size in all three source periods (median about 8 to 9 m). REVIEW: confirm the exact definition with the data owner.
Water depth at the haul point farthest from shore ('full distance out'), in meters, recorded in 1997-2001 data only (units per the 1997-2001 field datasheet).
Water depth at the haul point closest to shore, in meters, recorded in 1997-2001 data only (units per the 1997-2001 field datasheet).

Stream feature (mesohabitat unit) of the sampled area: Riffle (shallow, swift, turbulent water), Run, Glide (uniform channel bottom with moderate to low velocity and little turbulence) or Pool (slow, usually deep water), or a combination joined with '&' where more than one was recorded.

Seine area of the haul. REVIEW (defined differently between periods): 1997-2001 values are supplied in the source data and equal haul length x width (square meters); 2008-2025 values were calculated as length x width x average depth, which is a volume (cubic meters). Only 43 values exist for 2015-2025 and all are 0 because width is mostly missing. Confirm the intended definition before publishing.
Number of fish of this species (and length, where measured) in the record, including fish that were counted but not measured. Blank for 1997-2001 data, where each row is one individual fish.
missingValueCodeExplanation: Not recorded (1997-2001 rows are individual fish)

attributeDefinition: Average water depth of the haul, in meters. Source column 'bs_depth_1_2', confirmed by the data owner to be the average depth. Two entries missing a decimal point (samples 899 and 1066) were corrected. For 1997-2001 see depth_1 and depth_2.
missingValueCodeExplanation: Not recorded (1997-2001 data) or not entered

attributeDefinition: Weight of the fish, in grams, recorded in 2015-2025 data only. Per the survey report, a subsample of salmonids was weighed to the nearest 0.1 g if at least 40 mm fork length; weights were not collected during windy or heavy rain conditions because of inaccurate readings.
Calendar year of the sample, derived from date.

River mile of the standardized river-mile site assigned to the sampling location, measured in miles upstream from the Feather River's confluence with the Sacramento River at Verona (river mile 0); the Fish Barrier Dam is at river mile 67. Locations were assigned to a site using the program's Subsite Table, supplemented by manual assignments.

Number of seine hauls (pulls) made in the sample, parsed from free-text crew comments (e.g. '2 pulls'). Additional hauls may be made when a haul is rated poor. Blank when no count was stated in the comments, which does not imply a single haul.

Substrate types present in the sampled area, as comma-separated categories: Fine (small gravel, 0-50 mm), Small (medium gravel, 50-150 mm), Medium (large cobble, 150-300 mm), Boulder (>300 mm) or Pavement (boat ramp). All substrate present is recorded; the order listed does not indicate dominance.

Cover types present in the sampled area, as comma-separated categories (e.g. No Apparent Cover, Small Instream Objects/Woody Debris, Large Instream Objects/Woody Debris, Overhead Objects, Submerged Aquatic Veg/Algae, Undercut Bank). All cover present is recorded; the order listed does not indicate dominance.
Whether the fish had a clipped adipose fin (TRUE/FALSE), derived from the species entry in the source data. Blank where not applicable or not recorded.
